newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU revises up 1996/97 oilseed crop to 12.15 mln T.
newsitem.headline: EU revises up 1996/97 oilseed crop to 12.15 mln T.

text.p: The European Commission has revised its latest 1996/97 oilseed crop estimate upwards to 12.15 million tonnes, from 12.06 million.

In the latest estimates supplied to the Commission and obtained from a diplomatic source by Reuters, oilseed production for food use was put at 10.72 million tonnes compared with 10.61 million on October 25.
The balance was made up of oilseeds grown for energy and other non-food uses.
On November 5 Coceral, the EU grain traders' group, estimated 1996/97 oilseeds production at 12.26 million tonnes, against 12.61 million last season.
The Commission put the total rapeseed crop for the European Union 15 at 7.04 million tonnes but Coceral said it estimated the crop at 7.2 million tonnes.
The rapeseed production estimate compared with a figure of 6.94 million tonnes given to the last cereals and oilseeds management committee on October 25, but trade sources said it was too low.
The figure for total non-food oilseed production was down at 1.43 million tonnes compared with 1.45 million in the previous estimate.

"Both Germany and Greece complained that the estimates given to the management committee on October 25 were too high due to bad winter weather and a shift by farmers to wheat", a COCERAL official said.
Bad weather forced many German farmers to replant and many switched to wheat from summer rapeseed, COCERAL said.
